context: Round 3 builds Squire's set-up: from the download to the Squire's first reply, without Terminal, on a Squire owner's own Mac and under their own Claude sign-in. Three facts shape it. A fresh Mac has no usable Python until Apple's command line tools are installed (/usr/bin/python3 is then Apple's stub, which offers to install the tools rather than run Python), yet the Mac check and an unsupported Mac's refusal must run before anything changes. The plan is readable only through Claude Code after it is installed and signed in, which is itself a change to the Mac, so the plan check cannot come first. And the download is not signed by Apple, so macOS stops it once until the owner clicks Open Anyway in System Settings. Runtime facts below come from the documentation pages named (code.claude.com: setup, cli-reference, authentication, model-config, settings-reference, managed-settings, remote-control; support.apple.com/en-us/102445 for Gatekeeper; the man pages for launchd.plist, launchctl, codesign, xattr and sw_vers on macOS 26.3.1), from round 2's measured facts (ADR-003), from the probes run on a test user's Mac with Claude Code 2.1.319 on 2026-11-09 (each marked measured where it settles a fact), or are marked owed with the probe that settles them. Anything not stated outright by a source is marked inferred.
decision:
1. The download and its entry point. Squire's download is one per-user app, Squire.app, bundle identifier com.stravica.squire, that carries core: its own executable Contents/MacOS/Squire is the entry point, Contents/Info.plist names it, and Contents/Resources/core is core as released. In this repository the app's source is installer/Squire.app (its executable and Info.plist); the release puts core at Contents/Resources/core (the signed release bundle is round 4's), and a test world assembles the app the same way, a copy of installer/Squire.app with a copy of core/ at Contents/Resources/core. The executable is a zsh script (#!/bin/zsh): a bare macOS 13 has zsh, osascript, plutil and curl, needs no compiler for it, and its functions take Code Nodes. Everything before Apple's tools are present runs in it (lines 6 to 10); everything after runs core's Python, /usr/bin/python3 -B Contents/Resources/core/tools/set-up.py, started by the executable only once Apple's tools answer. Nothing of Squire's is fetched: Claude Code comes from its maker's installer and Apple's tools from Apple's own dialog. The app writes nothing inside itself.
2. Where set-up keeps things. The Squire home is SQUIRE_HOME when set, else ~/Library/Application Support/Squire, as core already reads it. Set-up's own record is set-up.json in the Squire home (line 13). Claude Code's config folder for Squire's session is claude-config in the Squire home (ADR-003 line 3); the sign-in goes there. The owner's folder is ~/Squire unless the owner picks another, never under Desktop, Documents, Downloads or iCloud Drive (macOS asks the owner before an app reads Desktop, Documents and Downloads: support.apple.com Mac help "Control access to files and folders on Mac"). Set-up writes ownerFolder, keychain (the login keychain, the production keychain from round 1) and backupFolder into the Squire home's squire.json, Squire's own config; and squireName and personality into the owner's squire.json, the file of that name at the top of the owner's folder, where the runner already reads squireName (ADR-003 line 7), keeping any other keys it holds.
3. The Mac's own commands, and how a test world reaches them. Set-up runs the Mac's own commands by name: sw_vers, sysctl, id, xcode-select, curl, bash, osascript, open and plutil, on the PATH it was opened with followed by /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin. Finder opens an app with launchd's PATH, which is those four folders (inferred), so on a Squire owner's Mac the commands are the Mac's own. Python is only ever /usr/bin/python3, and only after Apple's tools answer; claude is only ever found at the fixed places in ADR-003 line 5, never by PATH. A test world puts its own folder of fakes first on that PATH and runs the app's real executable as a process: the Mac check reads a fake sw_vers, a fake memory reading (sysctl -n hw.memsize), a fake group list (id -Gn) and a fake xcode-select; the download reads a fake curl that serves a fake Claude Code installer; the owner's answers come from a fake osascript that answers each window by its title; the browser is a fake open that records what it was asked to open. That answer source exists only in the test world; Squire ships no answer file and no switch for one.
4. Set-up's own windows. Each is an osascript dialog (display dialog, or choose from list for the plan), its title one of: "Squire: your Claude plan" (the declaration), "Squire: set up" (the one yes; buttons "Not now" and "Install"), "Squire: name your Squire" and "Squire: your Squire's personality" (each a default answer), "Squire: your plan" (the ask of line 9; buttons "Stop" and "Continue"), "Squire: your phone" (buttons "Later" and "Done"), "Squire: cannot set up" (a refusal before any change), "Squire: set-up stopped" (a stop after a change, and what was undone), "Squire: set-up paused" (a failure that leaves set-up to resume: what went wrong and to open Squire again) and "Squire: ready" (the end). Answers are read from osascript's own result: "button returned:<button>", with ", text returned:<text>" after a default answer; the chosen item for a list, or false when cancelled. Set-up never opens Terminal and never asks the owner to open anything but its own windows, the browser, System Settings and Apple's tools dialog; the Claude app is offered on the phone window, never required. On the Mac the owner talks to Squire at claude.ai/code in the default browser.
5. The steps, in order (readiness item 14's ten, in item 3's order), each with its id in the record: yes (the Mac check, the plan the owner declares and the one yes); claudeCode (Claude Code found or installed); signIn (the sign-in into Squire's config folder, then the plan read); appleTools; naming (the Squire's name and personality); ownerFolder; layDown (core laid down from the app's own core: the session and the wake-ups); backup (the nightly backup job); health (the health check); phone (optional); firstConversation. Item 14's second step, Claude Code and the sign-in, is recorded as two, claudeCode and signIn, so a sign-in that fails keeps Claude Code. The browser and voice-note steps are round 6's.
6. The Mac check, at every start of the app and before any write: macOS 13 or later (sw_vers -productVersion), 4 GB of memory or more (sysctl -n hw.memsize, 4294967296 bytes), both Claude Code's own floor (setup page, System requirements); and Apple's command line tools present (xcode-select -p answers, exit 0, naming a folder that exists) or installable by this user, which is an administrator (admin among id -Gn). A Mac that fails is refused before any write, on the "Squire: cannot set up" window, which names what is missing and the way on: an older macOS names macOS 13 and says to update macOS in System Settings; too little memory names 4 GB; a user who cannot install Apple's tools names Apple's command line tools and says to ask whoever administers this Mac to install them, or to set Squire up from an administrator's account. Each refusal leaves the home folder and every record exactly as found.
7. The declaration and the one yes, still before any write. The "Squire: your Claude plan" window lists Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise, Free, and I'm not sure. Free, or a cancelled window, is refused before any write on "Squire: cannot set up", naming Pro and the way on (a Pro plan or above at claude.ai, then open Squire again); I'm not sure goes on and the plan read decides (line 9). Then the one yes, "Squire: set up", names every piece set-up adds: Claude Code, with its own background updates (setup page, Auto-updates); Apple's command line tools, with the system's own administrator password prompt, when they are not already there; Squire itself; and each background job lay-down writes (the session runner, the wake-ups and the backup). Not now installs nothing, writes nothing and ends set-up. Install creates the Squire home and the record, and nothing outside the named list is ever installed.
8. Claude Code. Found when the fixed places of ADR-003 line 5 hold a claude, owned by the user and not writable by others, that answers claude --version (exit 0, a version: setup page, Verify your installation); then nothing is installed and it is never recorded as added. Otherwise set-up downloads the native installer with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh, bounded at 10 minutes, into a file of its own, and only when curl exits 0 runs it with bash (setup page, Native Install: the launcher at ~/.local/bin/claude is a link into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/; inferred: no administrator). Before downloading it records claudeCode in added, with each of ~/.local, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.local/state, ~/.local/state/claude, ~/.cache, ~/.cache/claude, ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json that did not exist, so an undo can leave the home as found (measured: besides the launcher and the versions folder the native installer makes ~/.claude, ~/.claude.json, ~/.cache/claude and ~/.local/state/claude under HOME, and writes no shell file). A download that fails, times out or is cut short runs no installer, leaves no launcher, records nothing done, and shows "Squire: set-up paused" naming the download and to open Squire again; the next run starts the step again from its start. Measured: run from a launchd job in the login session, with no terminal and no TTY, the documented command completed in 24 to 35 seconds, asked nothing, needed no administrator and opened no window; claude --version then printed "2.1.319 (Claude Code)". The real app runs with the owner's own HOME, where the probe used a folder of its own.
9. The sign-in and the plan read. Set-up runs claude auth login with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to Squire's config folder (cli-reference: claude auth login), which opens the browser's sign-in page (owed: the owner's own run on a test Mac); the sign-in is bounded at 15 minutes. Signed in means claude auth status in that folder exits 0 with loggedIn true and the folder's .claude.json holds oauthAccount (ADR-003 line 3; rulings: loggedIn alone was not enough). A sign-in that is cancelled, times out or has no internet is explained on "Squire: set-up paused" (the sign-in, and to open Squire again), keeps everything done before it, and the next run resumes at the sign-in with Claude Code kept. Then the plan read, from claude auth status in that folder: its subscriptionType field. Measured: 2.1.319 prints subscriptionType (a lower-case plan word, "max" on the one account seen) and planTier ("max_20x") beside the documented loggedIn, authMethod and configDirectory; neither is documented, so only the one value was seen. pro, max, ultra, team and enterprise go on (setup page: Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise or Console account). free is below Pro. A value set-up does not know, a missing field, or an answer it cannot read is asked on "Squire: your plan": "Squire could not confirm your plan; it needs Pro or above. Continue?"; Continue goes on, Stop is treated as below Pro. A plan below Pro stops set-up and undoes what set-up added: claude auth logout in Squire's config folder (cli-reference), then each entry in added, newest first (Claude Code's launcher and versions folder only when set-up installed them, then the folders it made, then the Squire home), leaving the home folder as set-up found it, never touching a Claude Code that was there before; "Squire: set-up stopped" names Pro and the way on. The plan read comes before Apple's tools and everything else system-wide, so the undo never needs an administrator.
10. Apple's command line tools. Present when xcode-select -p answers (line 6); then nothing is installed. Otherwise xcode-select --install opens Apple's own dialog and set-up waits for xcode-select -p to answer, looking every 10 seconds and at most 60 minutes. Tools not confirmed in that time are not recorded done; "Squire: set-up paused" says Apple's tools are not finished and to open Squire again, and the next run starts this step again from its start (that a script can start Apple's tools dialog is owed to the release Verify's from-zero run, TM3). Then the executable starts core's Python steps.
11. Naming, the owner's folder and lay-down. naming asks "Squire: name your Squire" and "Squire: your Squire's personality" and keeps both answers in set-up.json (squireName, personality). ownerFolder makes ~/Squire (or the folder picked) when absent, writes ownerFolder into the Squire home's squire.json and squireName and personality into the owner's squire.json; a folder already there is kept as it is, and an owner's squire.json already there keeps its other keys. layDown runs lay-down, /usr/bin/python3 -B <app>/Contents/Resources/core/tools/lay-down.py <app>/Contents/Resources/core, which lays core down, writes the config folder's settings and Squire's launchd agents and loads them only in the account's own home (ADR-003 line 2); set-up records the core folder it laid down from as release in set-up.json, for the known fixes (line 17).
12. The first conversation, and why a server stopped. firstConversation waits, at most 2 minutes, for the session: one session record whose process is alive and listens on its socket (ADR-003 lines 10 and 18), then opens https://claude.ai/code in the default browser (open) and shows "Squire: ready" naming the Squire. When the server stops before any session, the runner records the server's own last line in runner.json's problems ("no session: Claude Code's Remote Control server stopped before any session started: " then that line; round 2's TEST saw "Unable to determine your organization for Remote Control eligibility" on 12 of 12 starts with runner.json empty and the health check silent), the health check prints it, and set-up's last step names it on "Squire: set-up paused" and records nothing done. The guide for the first conversation (what Squire can do, how approval works, the privacy words, house style, fresh starts) is in the instructions lay-down writes (line 15); the reply that names the Squire is the Journey test's.
13. The record, each step's end state, the lock and the re-run. set-up.json in the Squire home is {"done": [the step ids done, in order], "added": [what set-up added], "release": <the core folder laid down from>}, written whole through a file beside it. Every step checks its end state before it starts and after it ends, is safe to run again, and is recorded done only when its end state is seen after it ends: yes, the record holds it; claudeCode, line 8's found test; signIn, line 9's signed-in test and a plan read that went on; appleTools, xcode-select -p answers; naming, both answers in set-up.json; ownerFolder, the folder exists, the Squire home's squire.json names it and the owner's squire.json holds squireName and personality; layDown, lay-down exited 0 and the installed core's digests match (ADR-003 line 6); backup, its agent is written; health, the health check exits 0 (the runner lay-down loaded is given up to 30 seconds to take its lock before the check counts it not running); phone, the owner answered; firstConversation, the browser was opened at claude.ai/code. A step whose end state cannot be confirmed (a launcher whose version folder is incomplete, Apple's tools still installing, a step killed part way) runs again from its start and is never counted done. One set-up at a time: an exclusive lock on squire-set-up.lock in the user's temporary folder (TMPDIR), taken after the Mac check and held until the app exits; a second set-up exits at once on "Squire: cannot set up", saying Squire's set-up is already running. Running the app again resumes at the first step not recorded done; a step recorded done whose end state no longer holds runs again; over a finished set-up it repairs what no longer holds and keeps the owner's folder and squire.json's settings. When the sign-in is gone, running the app again resumes at the sign-in step, and the health check's line for it says to open Squire's installer to sign in again. Uninstall is out of round 3.
14. The compaction window. core/settings.json carries "autoCompactWindow": 500000 (model-config: the auto-compact window; settings-reference: 100000 to 1000000 or "auto" from 2.1.288), laid into the config folder by lay-down, which the runner checks equal to core's before every start (ADR-003 lines 3 and 6); set-up reaches it by calling lay-down. Nothing is written to the owner's ~/.claude, whose settings, shell environment and command line never reach Squire's session (ADR-003 lines 3, 4 and 7). Measured: a session reading Squire's config folder reported its window through Claude Code's own /context as 500k with the key and 1m without it, on the same model (claude-haiku-5-5, read through claude -p with that folder); the Remote Control session started as the runner starts it loaded the same settings.json (its SessionStart hook ran from it) and gives no remote report of its window. So the key is the route, and the runner's CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=500000, the pre-ruled fallback, is not built. The update keys (autoUpdatesChannel stable, a minimumVersion floor) live in core's settings when they are built, in round 4 with Claude Code's own updates; round 3 binds no test to them. The health check reads every source it knows and names any value other than 500000, with its source: core's installed settings and the config folder's settings, each at the top level and per model under modelSettings; the session's environment as the runner's agent sets it; the managed settings file and its managed-settings.d folder in /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode; and the com.anthropic.claudecode managed preferences domain in /Library/Managed Preferences (managed-settings page). A managed source that exists but cannot be read gives "cannot confirm the compaction window", naming the source; never a pass and never silence. A model whose context window is below 500k is not drift: Claude Code caps the window at the model's (model-config), and the health check names no line for it. The health check reads those system places under the root /, and under SQUIRE_SYSTEM_ROOT when that is set: the test world's own folder, the one way a test reaches a place only an administrator can write (a switch that exists for the tests, listed for the owner to strike).
15. The name and personality. squireName and personality live in the owner's squire.json at the top of the owner's folder: the owner's own file, which set-up writes from the owner's answers and the session changes only with the owner's yes (the floor's rule for the owner's folder). Lay-down writes them into CLAUDE.md in the config folder, which Claude Code loads as the user's own instructions for Squire's session, at every lay-down, and the runner writes it again before every start; both carry them unchanged. Measured: a CLAUDE.md in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR loaded in a Remote Control session started as the runner starts it, listed in the session's own transcript as the user's instructions, and the session answered with the word only that file held. --name carries squireName (ADR-003 line 7). In round 3, "after Squire is updated" reads "after core is laid down again": the bound test lays a changed core down and finds both unchanged in what the session loads; round 4 proves it again through the signed update.
16. The nightly backup. core/tools/backup.py, run by its own launchd agent, com.stravica.squire.backup, which lay-down writes beside the other two (/usr/bin/python3 -B with the installed copy, SQUIRE_HOME in its environment, StartCalendarInterval at 02:30 every night, no KeepAlive; loaded only in the account's own home). It backs the owner's folder (ownerFolder) up into backupFolder from squire.json: by default the iCloud Drive folder ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Squire Backup; any folder in the test world. The backup holds current/, the owner's folder as it was at the last run, and archive/<UTC date and time of the run>/, one per run: a file removed from the owner's folder moves from current/ into that run's archive folder, and a changed file's earlier copy moves there before the new copy goes into current/; nothing in the backup is ever deleted or overwritten. The job creates backupFolder only when its parent exists, so with iCloud Drive off the destination is absent. A destination that is absent, not writable or full gives no partial pass: the job exits non-zero, records the run as failed in backup.json in the Squire home, and the health check prints a line naming the backup and the destination; the next night's run tries again in full, and a run that succeeds clears the line. Measured: a LaunchAgent's /usr/bin/python3 made, wrote, read back and removed a folder directly under the home (beside ~/Squire) with no prompt; it did the same in the iCloud Drive folder of a user with iCloud Drive on, with no prompt; that the copy then syncs was not observed (the probe file lived under a second). Real sync is a by-hand line of the Journey walk and the release Verify.
17. The known fixes, from the health check's own lines, each checked by the health check itself rather than read from the runner's last record: the runner not running (no runner holds its lock in the Squire home): reload Squire's agents; a floor file changed (an installed floor file differs from its digest): lay core down again from the release in set-up.json; not signed in (claude auth status in the config folder does not answer signed in): open Squire's installer to sign in again, a fix the owner makes, which changes nothing by itself; a moved settings file: named only, it is the owner's file, and no fix is offered. The health check prints each fault's line and, for a fix that changes anything, the command that applies it: /usr/bin/python3 <Squire home>/core/tools/health.py --fix runner or --fix floor. The session runs that command, so the floor asks the owner for it and it runs only after the owner's yes (ADR-001's approvals); the fix then runs the check again and says plainly when the fault is still there. Measured at round 3's base: the floor refuses that command as a change to Squire's core, yes or no, so the floor gains one exception, exactly these two commands (/usr/bin/python3 with the installed health.py in the Squire home and --fix runner or --fix floor, nothing more on the line), which it asks the owner for; every other command that would change Squire's core stays refused, yes or no. The new health lines (the known fixes, the compaction window and the backup) are named for an installed Squire, one whose core is laid down in the Squire home; a Squire home with no core laid down is checked as rounds 1 and 2 left it. A fault not on the list (an ignored overlay, a server that stopped before any session, a backup that could not run) is named and nothing is offered. Round 3 prints lines; the page is round 6's and the ticket is round 4's.
18. The phone and the end. phone shows "Squire: your phone", how to install the Claude app on the phone and sign in to the same Claude account, and is done on either answer: set-up completes with no phone, and the phone can join later. Closing the laptop or quitting during the first conversation leaves every earlier step done; the session resumes under the same session id (ADR-003 line 11), so the conversation goes on where it stopped, and running the app again finishes the last step.
19. What the no-Terminal release check and the Journey test read on a target Mac, over SSH as the Squire owner's user. The window list: CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo through osascript -l JavaScript gives each on-screen window's owning process id, owner name and layer, with no permission held (titles are withheld without Screen Recording, and none is asked for); lsappinfo info -only bundleid <pid> gives the owning app's bundle identifier (measured). Application windows are layer 0. During set-up every new layer-0 window must belong to the allow-list: Squire's app (com.stravica.squire) or a process it started, the default browser (the https handler LaunchServices names, and Safari), System Settings (com.apple.systempreferences), Gatekeeper's own message (com.apple.coreservices.uiagent), Apple's tools dialog (com.apple.dt.CommandLineTools.installondemand) and the Claude app (com.anthropic.claudefordesktop); any other app's window fails, and a window whose owner has no bundle identifier the check can read fails. A hidden terminal session with no window is inside the promise. Set-up's progress is read from set-up.json in the target's Squire home; the session from its record (ADR-003 line 18); the first reply from the session's own transcript in the config folder.
consequences:
Usage model for the budgets and timeouts the criteria and steps carry; every figure is an assumption unless a source is named.
The 500k compaction window. Typical: a Squire owner's day is a few short conversations and wake-ups in one long session; the session compacts at 500k tokens and never grows into a 1M-token session, so each turn after a compaction costs at most about half what a full 1M context would (model-config: the window is capped at the model's own). Heavy: a long research job fills the window several times a day; each fill costs one compaction, and the health check names any setting that would lift the window. A model with a smaller context runs at its own window, which costs less.
The nightly backup. Typical: an owner's folder of a few thousand small files and a few hundred MB, a few dozen changed files a night; one run copies the changes in seconds to minutes. Heavy: a first run over tens of GB, or a night with thousands of changed files; the run takes as long as the copy, and missed nights (the Mac asleep at 02:30) are coalesced by launchd into one run on waking (man launchd.plist, StartCalendarInterval). The archive grows by every changed or removed file and is never pruned in round 3.
Set-up's timeouts. The download: typical seconds to a minute for Claude Code's installer and binary; heavy, a slow connection, bounded at 10 minutes, then paused to resume. The sign-in: typical one to two minutes in the browser; heavy, the owner steps away, bounded at 15 minutes, then paused to resume. Apple's tools: typical 5 to 15 minutes from Apple's dialog; heavy, a slow connection or a dialog left unanswered, bounded at 60 minutes, then paused to resume. The session at the last step: typical seconds (round 2's walk: the record 5 seconds after lay-down); heavy, a refused account or a slow first start, bounded at 2 minutes, then the server's reason or a pause.
Accepted residuals, written at round 3's open (none ships past the release Verify unruled): (a) between an approved settings write and the runner's stop, a tool call may run without the floor; (b) an approved program holding the session's messaging token could post a bare yes; (c) a write the floor cannot resolve, once allowed, can reach the approvals ledger; (d) a program that reaches /usr/bin/security indirectly after one yes can print a secret, accepted for v0.1. Also: the floor digests do not yet cover core/lib/squire.py, and a job with no record keeps no marks until its first mark.
Set-up runs the Mac's commands on the PATH it is opened with (line 3): a program already running as the owner could put its own sw_vers or curl first on that PATH, which needs code already running as the owner; Python and claude are never looked up on PATH.
The Gatekeeper click (Open Anyway in System Settings, Privacy and Security, then Open: support.apple.com/en-us/102445) is a by-hand line of the Journey walk and the release Verify, never a bound assertion; whether it is offered for an ad-hoc-signed, quarantined app whose executable is a zsh script on macOS 26 is owed (the owner's own run on a test Mac). That the sign-in opens the browser from the app with no terminal and lands in Squire's config folder is owed (the owner's own run on a test Mac). Real iCloud, Apple's tools from a script (TM3) and a from-zero Mac are the release Verify's.

alternativesConsidered.name: An installer package (.pkg)
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship set-up as a package whose scripts run as root after an administrator password.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Every owner would need an administrator password, the scripts run as root outside the owner's login session where Squire's agents live, and the per-user pieces (Claude Code, the config folder, the agents) need no administrator.

alternativesConsidered.name: The app fetches core from a release asset
alternativesConsidered.summary: Download core at set-up instead of carrying it.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It would depend on round 4's signed release and its checks before they exist; carrying core keeps round 3 to what is proven here.

alternativesConsidered.name: The first step in Swift
alternativesConsidered.summary: A Swift executable built for macOS 13 for the Mac check and the steps before Python.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It needs a build step and a toolchain in the release, and its checks take Code Nodes only on a class or a binding; zsh, osascript, plutil and curl are already on a bare macOS 13.

alternativesConsidered.name: The first step in Python
alternativesConsidered.summary: Run core's Python from the start.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: On a fresh Mac /usr/bin/python3 is Apple's stub until Apple's tools are installed, so the Mac check and its refusal could not run before a change.

alternativesConsidered.name: Check the plan before anything changes
alternativesConsidered.summary: Refuse a plan below Pro before any change, as first worded.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The plan is readable only through Claude Code after it is installed and signed in; the owner's declaration stops before any change and the read after sign-in undoes what set-up added.

alternativesConsidered.name: Read the plan only after the sign-in
alternativesConsidered.summary: No declaration; only the read, with the undo.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: An owner who knows their plan is below Pro would see Claude Code installed and removed for nothing.

alternativesConsidered.name: Install Apple's tools before Claude Code
alternativesConsidered.summary: Apple's tools first, so Python runs the rest.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: They are system-wide and cannot be removed without an administrator, so a plan found below Pro afterwards could not leave the Mac as set-up found it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Require an administrator for everyone
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A standard user on a Mac that already has Apple's tools needs no administrator; only one without them is refused, with the way on.

alternativesConsidered.name: A transaction that rolls every step back
alternativesConsidered.summary: Undo the whole set-up on any failure.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Steps such as Apple's tools and a browser sign-in cannot be rolled back cleanly; steps that check their own end state and run again on doubt resume or repair the one installation.

alternativesConsidered.name: Write the window into the owner's ~/.claude settings
alternativesConsidered.summary: Where the first plan put the 500k key.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Squire's session reads only its own config folder (ADR-003 line 3), so the key would never reach it.

alternativesConsidered.name: The environment variable as the only window route
alternativesConsidered.summary: Set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW in the runner and nothing in settings.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: One route already guarded by the runner's equality check and the digests is enough if the key reaches the session; measured, the key reaches the session, so the variable is not needed.

alternativesConsidered.name: Refuse to start the session on any doubt about the window
alternativesConsidered.summary: No session while a source cannot be read.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A managed file the owner cannot read would leave them with no Squire; the health check says it cannot confirm the window instead.

alternativesConsidered.name: Watch for Terminal by name
alternativesConsidered.summary: A deny-list of terminal apps for the no-Terminal check.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It decides only the instances listed; the release check allows only the expected apps and fails anything else, and anything it cannot classify.

alternativesConsidered.name: The name and personality only in the Squire home, or a model-judged reply test
alternativesConsidered.summary: Other placements and proofs for the persona.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Kept in squire.json they stay the owner's; whether a reply uses a personality is a judgement, so the bound test reads what the session loads and the Journey test reads the first reply for the name.

alternativesConsidered.name: Back up somewhere other than iCloud Drive, or only the two listed cases
alternativesConsidered.summary: Other destinations or a narrower backup.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: iCloud Drive is what the owner approved; a backup that silently does nothing when iCloud is off, or overwrites a changed file, breaks the promise without a sign.

alternativesConsidered.name: A yes per piece, or a separate sign-in-again app
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The story asks for one yes for what will be installed; running the same app again resumes at the sign-in, so no second app is needed.

alternativesConsidered.name: Read managed settings through the Mac's preference commands
alternativesConsidered.summary: Have the health check shell out to defaults or plutil for the managed sources so a fake on PATH could answer.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It would add commands only for the tests' sake; one root for the system places is smaller and is listed for the owner.

title: The set-up app: one download carrying core, steps that check their own end state, the plan checked by declaration and by sign-in, and the settings, persona, backup and known fixes it lays down
